chapters.title: For Three Transgressions, and for Four
chapters.html:
Amos 1

The LORD Roars from Zion

1The words of Amos, one of the sheep breeders from Tekoa: what he saw concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.

2He said:
The LORD roars from Zion
and utters His voice from Jerusalem;
the pastures of the shepherds mourn,
and the top of Carmel dries up.

Damascus

3This is what the LORD says:
For three transgressions of Damascus,
and for four, I will not turn it back,
because they threshed Gilead
with threshing sledges of iron.

4I will send fire on the house of Hazael,
and it will devour the strongholds of Ben-hadad.

5I will break the bar of Damascus,
and cut off the one enthroned from the Valley of Aven,
and the one who holds the scepter from Beth-eden;
and the people of Aram will go into exile to Kir,
says the LORD.

Gaza

6This is what the LORD says:
For three transgressions of Gaza,
and for four, I will not turn it back,
because they took a whole people into exile
to hand them over to Edom.

7I will send fire on the wall of Gaza,
and it will devour her strongholds.

8I will cut off the one enthroned from Ashdod,
and the one who holds the scepter from Ashkelon;
I will turn My hand against Ekron,
and the remnant of the Philistines will perish,
says the Lord GOD.

Tyre

9This is what the LORD says:
For three transgressions of Tyre,
and for four, I will not turn it back,
because they handed over a whole people to Edom
and did not remember the covenant of brothers.

10I will send fire on the wall of Tyre,
and it will devour her strongholds.

Edom

11This is what the LORD says:
For three transgressions of Edom,
and for four, I will not turn it back,
because he pursued his brother with the sword
and destroyed his compassion;
his anger tore without end,
and he kept his wrath forever.

12I will send fire on Teman,
and it will devour the strongholds of Bozrah.

Ammon

13This is what the LORD says:
For three transgressions of the Ammonites,
and for four, I will not turn it back,
because they ripped open the pregnant women of Gilead
to enlarge their territory.

14I will kindle a fire on the wall of Rabbah,
and it will devour her strongholds,
with a war cry on the day of battle,
with a storm on the day of the whirlwind.

15Their king will go into exile,
he and his princes together,
says the LORD.

Notes

  • v1 "one of the sheep breeders from Tekoa… two years before the earthquake" — noqedim, the word used of a king: Now Mesha king of Moab was a sheep breeder (2 Kings 3:4). Tekoa was a town of Judah, one of the cities Rehoboam built for defense in Judah (2 Chronicles 11:5–6), but the words concern Israel, the north. The kings are those of Hosea 1:1, Uzziah of Judah and Jeroboam son of Joash. The earthquake is remembered again in Zechariah 14:5. The Greek reads noqedim as a place, in Akkarim in Thekoue, and has concerning Jerusalem.

  • v2 "The LORD roars from Zion" — yish'ag, the roar of a lion. In Hosea 11:10 He will roar like a lion to call His sons home; here the roar dries up the land. Jeremiah has the same picture in his own words, The LORD will roar from on high, and utter His voice from His holy dwelling (Jeremiah 25:30), and Joel has the two lines word for word (Joel 3:16). Avlu, mourn, is said of land as well as people, as in How long will the land mourn, and the grass of every field wither? (Jeremiah 12:4).

  • v3 "For three transgressions of Damascus, and for four, I will not turn it back" — the refrain of eight oracles, word for word each time (1:3, 6, 9, 11, 13; 2:1, 4, 6). Three, then four, is a way of counting to the full number, as in In six troubles He will deliver you; in seven no evil will touch you (Job 5:19); yet for Damascus, Gaza, Ammon and Moab the charge that follows names a single deed. Pesha, transgression, is rebellion, the verb of Moab rebelled against Israel (2 Kings 1:1). Lo ashivennu, I will not turn it back: it is never named. The words are Balaam's of a blessing, He has blessed, and I cannot turn it back (Numbers 23:20). The Greek has I will not turn away from him.

  • vv3–4 "they threshed Gilead with threshing sledges of iron… the house of Hazael… Ben-hadad" — Hazael of Damascus struck them throughout all the territory of Israel, from the Jordan eastward, all the land of Gilead (2 Kings 10:32–33), and left Israel's army like the dust at threshing (2 Kings 13:7); Ben-hadad was his son. The Greek reads the crime as they sawed with iron saws the pregnant women of Gilead. I will send fire on… and it will devour… strongholds is the line Hosea uses of Judah's cities (Hosea 8:14).

  • v5 "the Valley of Aven… Beth-eden… Kir" — Aven is wickedness, the word of Beth-aven (Hosea 4:15); Eden is delight. Yoshev, the one enthroned, is the one who sits: an inhabitant, or a king on his throne, as in He who sits in the heavens (Psalm 2:4); the next line has the scepter. Kir is where the king of Assyria carried its people into exile when he took Damascus (2 Kings 16:9).

  • vv6, 9 "a whole people… to hand them over to Edom" — galut shelemah, a whole exile, a people taken entire and sold on. The Greek reads shelemah as Shelomoh: the captivity of Solomon. Gaza took them captive (v6); Tyre handed them over (v9).

  • v8 "Ashdod… Ashkelon… Ekron" — with Gaza, four of the five Philistine cities of 1 Samuel 6:17; Gath is not named. I will turn My hand against is Isaiah's I will turn My hand against you (Isaiah 1:25). The Lord GOD, Adonai YHWH, closes this oracle; Damascus, Ammon and Moab close with says the LORD.

  • v9 "did not remember the covenant of brothers" — berit achim. Hiram of Tyre and Solomon made a covenant (1 Kings 5:12), and Hiram called Solomon my brother (1 Kings 9:13).

  • v11 "he pursued his brother with the sword and destroyed his compassion" — Edom is Esau's people, and the law calls him brother: A message from your brother Israel (Numbers 20:14); You shall not detest an Edomite, for he is your brother (Deuteronomy 23:7). Rachamav, his compassion, is from rechem, womb: the feeling of those born of one womb, and these two were twins, Two nations are in your belly (Genesis 25:23). Va-yitrof, tore, is the verb of a beast with its prey, Torn, Joseph is torn (Genesis 37:33). Teman and Bozrah are named with Edom in Jeremiah (49:7, 13).

  • vv13–15 "ripped open the pregnant women of Gilead… Their king will go into exile" — the deed Elisha foresaw for Hazael, rip open their pregnant women (2 Kings 8:12). Sufah, whirlwind, is the word of they will reap the whirlwind (Hosea 8:7). Malkam, their king: Jeremiah, speaking against Ammon in nearly the same words, has for Milcom will go into exile, his priests and his princes together (Jeremiah 49:3), Milcom being the god of the sons of Ammon (1 Kings 11:33). Here the Hebrew names no priests, only princes, and the Greek has their kings… their priests and their princes.

chapters.title: Sold for a Pair of Sandals
chapters.html:
Amos 2

Moab

1This is what the LORD says:
For three transgressions of Moab,
and for four, I will not turn it back,
because he burned the bones of the king of Edom to lime.

2I will send fire on Moab,
and it will devour the strongholds of Kerioth;
Moab will die in the uproar,
with a war cry, with the sound of the horn.

3I will cut off the ruler from among her
and kill all her princes with him,
says the LORD.

Judah

4This is what the LORD says:
For three transgressions of Judah,
and for four, I will not turn it back,
because they rejected the law of the LORD
and did not keep His statutes;
their lies led them astray,
the lies their fathers followed.

5I will send fire on Judah,
and it will devour the strongholds of Jerusalem.

Israel

6This is what the LORD says:
For three transgressions of Israel,
and for four, I will not turn it back,
because they sell the righteous for silver,
and the needy for a pair of sandals.

7They trample the head of the poor
into the dust of the earth,
and turn aside the way of the humble;
a man and his father go to the same girl,
and so profane My holy name.

8They stretch out beside every altar
on garments taken in pledge,
and in the house of their God they drink
the wine of those who have been fined.

9Yet it was I who destroyed the Amorite before them,
whose height was like the height of the cedars,
and who was as strong as the oaks;
I destroyed his fruit above
and his roots below.

10It was I who brought you up from the land of Egypt
and led you in the wilderness forty years,
to take possession of the land of the Amorite.

11I raised up some of your sons as prophets
and some of your young men as Nazirites.
Is it not so, sons of Israel?
declares the LORD.

12But you made the Nazirites drink wine,
and you commanded the prophets, saying,
"You shall not prophesy."

13I am about to press you down in your place,
as a cart full of sheaves presses down.

14Flight will fail the swift;
the strong will not muster his strength,
and the warrior will not save his life.

15The one who handles the bow will not stand;
the swift of foot will not escape,
and the horseman will not save his life.

16The bravest of heart among the warriors
will flee naked on that day,
declares the LORD.

Notes

  • v1 "he burned the bones of the king of Edom to lime" — the charge against Moab is a wrong done to Edom, not to Israel. Sid, lime, is the word of plaster them with plaster (Deuteronomy 27:2): the bones burned down to powder. Moab and Edom were at war in the days of Elisha, when the king of Moab tried to break through to the king of Edom, but they could not (2 Kings 3:26).

  • vv2–3 "the strongholds of Kerioth… the ruler" — Kerioth is a town of Moab in Jeremiah, Kerioth is taken, and the strongholds are seized (Jeremiah 48:41); ha-qeriyyot can also be read the cities. Sha'on, uproar, is Jeremiah's word for Moab, the crown of the sons of tumult (Jeremiah 48:45). Shofet, the ruler, is the word for a judge, used here of the one who rules Moab.

  • vv4–5 "they rejected the law of the LORD… their lies led them astray" — the nations are charged with what they did to other peoples; Judah is charged with the law, as Hosea charged the north, Because you have rejected knowledge… since you have forgotten the law of your God (Hosea 4:6). Kizveihem, their lies, are the gods that failed them, and the fathers followed them first. The fire comes to Jerusalem in the words of the oracles before it.

  • v6 "they sell the righteous for silver, and the needy for a pair of sandals" — tsaddiq is the one in the right in a case, as in declaring the righteous one righteous and the wicked one wicked (Deuteronomy 25:1). Sold for silver, he loses his case to a bribe, or he is sold for his debt; for a pair of sandals, ba'avur na'alayim, puts the price of a man at what is worn on the feet. The eighth oracle is Israel's, and only Israel's charge runs past one verse, through v8.

  • v7 "They trample the head of the poor into the dust of the earth" — ha-sho'afim: the verb is trample in the psalm, man tramples on me (Psalm 56:1), and the Greek has treading. It is also pant, as in they pant for air like jackals (Jeremiah 14:6); read that way, the line is who pant after the dust of the earth on the head of the poor, men greedy even for the dust a mourner puts on his head, as the elders of Israel put dust on their heads (Joshua 7:6). Amos uses the word again in 8:4.

  • v7 "a man and his father go to the same girl, and so profane My holy name" — na'arah, a girl; the Greek has the same servant girl. The law kept a slave girl given to a son from his father: If he designates her for his son, he shall do for her according to the ruling for daughters (Exodus 21:9). To profane My holy name is the law's own sentence, You shall not profane My holy name (Leviticus 22:32).

  • v8 "garments taken in pledge… the wine of those who have been fined" — the law said of a poor man's cloak, If you take your neighbor's cloak as a pledge, you shall return it to him before the sun goes down (Exodus 22:26). Here they sleep on it beside the altar. Anushim, those who have been fined, is the verb of the law's penalty, he shall be fined (Exodus 21:22): the wine comes from fines, and it is drunk in the house of their God.

  • vv9–10 "the Amorite… his fruit above and his roots below… brought you up from the land of Egypt" — the scouts said, all the people we saw in it are men of great size (Numbers 13:32). His fruit above and his roots below is the reverse of Isaiah's promise to Judah, take root downward and bear fruit upward (Isaiah 37:31): the Amorite was destroyed from the top and the bottom both. The conquest is told in v9 before the exodus in v10. Forty years is Moses' count, I have led you forty years in the wilderness (Deuteronomy 29:5).

  • vv11–12 "you made the Nazirites drink wine… You shall not prophesy" — the Nazirite shall keep apart from wine and strong drink (Numbers 6:3). The two gifts of v11 are undone one each in v12: the Nazirite given wine, the prophet given silence. Amos himself is told not to prophesy at Bethel (7:12–13).

  • vv13–16 "I am about to press you down… Flight will fail the swift… flee naked on that day" — me'iq, press, is found only in this verse, from the root of the pressure of the wicked (Psalm 55:3); the Greek has I roll under you, as a wagon full of straw rolls. Ve-avad manos mi-qal, flight will fail the swift, is Jeremiah's line, Flight will fail the shepherds (Jeremiah 25:35). Seven fighters are named in vv14–16, from the swift to the bravest of heart, and not one escapes.

chapters.title: The Lion Has Roared
chapters.html:
Amos 3

Only You Have I Known

1Hear this word that the LORD has spoken against you, sons of Israel, against the whole family that I brought up from the land of Egypt:

2Only you have I known
of all the families of the ground;
therefore I will punish you
for all your iniquities.

The Lion Has Roared

3Do two walk together
unless they have agreed to meet?

4Does a lion roar in the forest
when it has no prey?
Does a young lion utter its voice from its den
unless it has caught something?

5Does a bird fall into a trap on the ground
when there is no lure for it?
Does a trap spring up from the ground
and catch nothing?

6If a horn is blown in a city,
do the people not tremble?
If disaster comes to a city,
has the LORD not done it?

7For the Lord GOD does nothing
unless He has revealed His counsel
to His servants the prophets.

8The lion has roared;
who will not fear?
The Lord GOD has spoken;
who will not prophesy?

The Mountains of Samaria

9Proclaim it over the strongholds in Ashdod
and over the strongholds in the land of Egypt,
and say: Gather on the mountains of Samaria,
and see the great tumults in her
and the oppressions within her.

10They do not know how to do what is right,
declares the LORD,
those who store up violence and destruction
in their strongholds.

11Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says:
An enemy will surround the land;
he will bring down your strength from you,
and your strongholds will be plundered.

12This is what the LORD says:
As the shepherd rescues from the lion's mouth
two legs or a piece of an ear,
so the sons of Israel who live in Samaria will be rescued,
with the corner of a bed
and a piece of a couch.

13Hear, and testify against the house of Jacob,
declares the Lord GOD, the God of hosts:

14On the day I punish Israel for its transgressions,
I will punish the altars of Bethel;
the horns of the altar will be cut off
and fall to the ground.

15I will strike the winter house
together with the summer house;
the houses of ivory will perish,
and the many houses will come to an end,
declares the LORD.

Notes

  • vv1–2 "the whole family that I brought up… Only you have I known of all the families of the ground" — mishpechot ha-adamah, the words of the promise to Abraham, In you all the families of the ground shall be blessed (Genesis 12:3). Yada'ti, I have known, is the knowing of a choice, as of Abraham, For I have known him, so that he may charge his sons (Genesis 18:19). The Hebrew puts only you first, and draws from it the opposite of a privilege: therefore I will punish you. The verse begins the LORD has spoken and turns, without a break, into the LORD's own I brought up.

  • vv3–6 "Do two walk together unless they have agreed to meet?" — seven questions, each with an answer everyone knows, before the answer that matters in vv7–8. No'adu, agreed to meet, is the verb of I will meet with you there (Exodus 25:22), the root of the tent of meeting; the Greek has unless they know each other. The two who walk together are not named.

  • v4 "Does a lion roar… Does a young lion utter its voice" — the words of the book's first oracle, The LORD roars from Zion and utters His voice from Jerusalem (1:2). The riddle is answered in v8: The lion has roared. Kefir, young lion, is Hosea's word as well (Hosea 5:14).

  • v6 "If disaster comes to a city, has the LORD not done it?" — ra'ah, disaster, the word of Isaiah's I make peace and create disaster (Isaiah 45:7). The horn is the alarm Hosea sounds too, Blow the horn in Gibeah (Hosea 5:8).

  • v7 "His counsel to His servants the prophets" — sod, the counsel of a closed circle, the word of Jeremiah's who has stood in the council of the LORD, to see and to hear His word? (Jeremiah 23:18). His servants the prophets is the phrase of I have sent you all My servants the prophets (Jeremiah 7:25). The Greek has instruction for sod.

  • vv9–10 "the strongholds in Ashdod… store up violence and destruction in their strongholds" — armenot, the strongholds the fire devoured in every oracle of 1:4–2:5, three times here: the strongholds of the nations are called to look at the strongholds of Samaria. The Greek has Assyria for Ashdod, the pair that Hosea gives, Egypt and Assyria (Hosea 7:11). Chamas va-shod, violence and destruction, is Jeremiah's cry, violence and destruction are heard in her (Jeremiah 6:7). Ha-otsrim, those who store up, is the verb of a treasury.

  • v11 "An enemy will surround the land" — tsar u-sevivh ha-arets, word for word an enemy, and around the land, with no verb. The Greek reads tsar as Tsor, Tyre: Tyre! your land will be laid waste all around.

  • v12 "As the shepherd rescues from the lion's mouth two legs or a piece of an ear" — the shepherd's law: If it was torn by a beast, he shall bring it as evidence (Exodus 22:13), as Jacob told Laban, Torn flesh I did not bring to you (Genesis 31:39). What the shepherd rescues proves the sheep is dead. U-vi-dmeshek arash, and a piece of a couch: demeshek is found only here, spelled with the letters of Damascus but with other vowels and a shin where Damascus has a sin (1:3; 5:27), and its meaning is not known; the line beside it, the corner of a bed, asks for a part of a couch. The Greek reads it as the city: in Damascus, which Jeroboam had restored… to Judah in Israel (2 Kings 14:28).

  • v14 "I will punish the altars of Bethel; the horns of the altar will be cut off" — the altar of Bethel was condemned before, when a man of God came out of Judah by the word of the LORD to Bethel: the altar shall be torn apart (1 Kings 13:1, 3). Amos too is from Judah (1:1). The horns of the altar were the place of refuge, where Adonijah took hold of the horns of the altar (1 Kings 1:50); cut off, they leave none.

  • v15 "the winter house… the houses of ivory… the many houses" — kings kept both: The king was sitting in the winter house (Jeremiah 36:22), and Ahab built the ivory house (1 Kings 22:39). Battim rabbim, many houses, is Isaiah's oath, Surely many houses shall be desolate, large and fine ones (Isaiah 5:9).

chapters.title: Prepare to Meet Your God
chapters.html:
Amos 4

The Cows of Bashan

1Hear this word, you cows of Bashan
who are on the mountain of Samaria,
who oppress the poor,
who crush the needy,
who say to their husbands,
"Bring, so that we may drink!"

2The Lord GOD has sworn by His holiness:
days are coming upon you
when they will carry you away with hooks,
and the last of you with fishhooks.

3You will go out through the breaches,
each woman straight ahead,
and you will be thrown out toward Harmon,
declares the LORD.

Yet You Did Not Return to Me

4Come to Bethel and transgress;
to Gilgal, and multiply transgression;
bring your sacrifices every morning,
your tithes every three days.

5Turn a thanksgiving offering of leavened bread into smoke,
and proclaim freewill offerings; announce them;
for that is what you love, sons of Israel,
declares the Lord GOD.

6I in turn gave you clean teeth in all your cities
and lack of bread in all your places;
yet you did not return to Me,
declares the LORD.

7I also withheld the rain from you
when there were still three months to the harvest;
I would send rain on one city
and send no rain on another city;
one field would be rained on,
and the field that had no rain would wither.

8Two or three cities would stagger to one city
to drink water, and would not be satisfied;
yet you did not return to Me,
declares the LORD.

9I struck you with scorching and mildew;
the locust devoured your many gardens and vineyards,
your fig trees and your olive trees;
yet you did not return to Me,
declares the LORD.

10I sent among you a plague, as in Egypt;
I killed your young men with the sword,
along with your captured horses;
I made the stench of your camps rise
into your nostrils;
yet you did not return to Me,
declares the LORD.

11I overthrew some of you,
as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah,
and you were like a brand snatched from the burning;
yet you did not return to Me,
declares the LORD.

Prepare to Meet Your God

12Therefore this is what I will do to you, Israel;
because I will do this to you,
prepare to meet your God, Israel!

13For He is the One who forms the mountains
and creates the wind,
who declares to man what His thought is,
who makes the dawn into darkness
and treads on the heights of the earth:
the LORD, the God of hosts, is His name.

Notes

  • v1 "you cows of Bashan… who say to their husbands" — Bashan, east of the Jordan, was known for its herds: rams, the breed of Bashan (Deuteronomy 32:14); strong bulls of Bashan (Psalm 22:12). The cows are the women of Samaria, and adoneihem, their lords, are their husbands, as Sarah says my husband is old (Genesis 18:12). Oppress and crush, ashaq and ratsats, are the two verbs of Samuel's defense, Whom have I cheated? Whom have I oppressed? (1 Samuel 12:3).

  • v2 "sworn by His holiness… with hooks, and the last of you with fishhooks" — the oath of Once for all I have sworn by My holiness (Psalm 89:35). Tsinnot and sirot dugah are uncertain: hooks and fishhooks, or baskets and fish-pots; sirot is elsewhere pots, and the Greek has they will take you with weapons, and those with you they will throw into cauldrons.

  • v3 "through the breaches… toward Harmon" — peratsim, the gaps broken in a taken city's wall, each woman going straight out through the one in front of her. Ha-Harmonah, toward Harmon, is a place named nowhere else, and where it was is not known; the Greek has the mountain Romman.

  • vv4–5 "Come to Bethel and transgress… your tithes every three days… leavened bread into smoke" — a call to worship, turned: pish'u, transgress, is the verb of the transgressions of 1:3–2:6. The law asked a tithe at the end of three years (Deuteronomy 14:28); here it is every three days. A thanksgiving offering came with loaves of leavened bread (Leviticus 7:13), but you shall not turn any sourdough… into smoke (Leviticus 2:11). They bring more than the law asks and the wrong thing, and that is what you love.

  • vv6–9 "yet you did not return to Me" — five times, after each blow (vv6, 8, 9, 10, 11). Ve-lo shavtem adai: ad, all the way to, the word of Hosea's call, Return, Israel, to the LORD your God (Hosea 14:1). Clean teeth are teeth with nothing to chew. The blows are those of Solomon's prayer at the temple, When the heavens are shut up and there is no rain… and turn from their sin (1 Kings 8:35), and if there is plague, scorching or mildew, locust (8:37); there the people are to turn, and here they do not. Na'u, stagger, is the drunkard's reeling of Psalm 107:27.

  • v10 "a plague, as in Egypt" — be-derekh Mitsrayim, Isaiah's as in Egypt (Isaiah 10:24). Dever, plague, struck Egypt's herds, a very heavy plague (Exodus 9:3), and the law threatened all the diseases of Egypt (Deuteronomy 28:60): the blows that brought Israel out now fall on Israel.

  • v11 "as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah… a brand snatched from the burning" — ke-mahpekhat Elohim et Sedom ve-et Amorah, the formula Jeremiah uses, As when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah (Jeremiah 50:40); it keeps God even in the LORD's own speech. The brand pulled from the fire is named again in Zechariah 3:2.

  • v12 "this is what I will do to you… prepare to meet your God" — what this is, the verse never says. Hikkon liqrat Elohekha are the words of Sinai: Be ready for three days (Exodus 19:15), when Moses brought the people out of the camp to meet God (Exodus 19:17). The meeting Israel was once made ready for is set again, after five refusals.

  • v13 "who declares to man what His thought is… the LORD, the God of hosts, is His name" — mah secho, what his thought is, names no one: God declaring His own thought, as He reveals His counsel to His servants the prophets (3:7), or showing a man his own. The Greek has announcing to men His anointed; meshicho, His anointed, has nearly the same letters. Oseh shachar efah, maker of dawn, darkness, has no and and no into; the Greek has who makes dawn and mist. The heights of the earth are those Moses sang of, He made him ride on the heights of the earth (Deuteronomy 32:13). The same ending closes 5:8, and again 9:6.

The Cows of Bashan
Hear this word, you cows of Bashan who are on the mountain of Samaria, who oppress the poor, who crush the needy, who say to their husbands, "Bring, so that we may drink!"
The Lord GOD has sworn by His holiness: days are coming upon you when they will carry you away with hooks, and the last of you with fishhooks.
You will go out through the breaches, each woman straight ahead, and you will be thrown out toward Harmon, declares the LORD.
Yet You Did Not Return to Me
Come to Bethel and transgress; to Gilgal, and multiply transgression; bring your sacrifices every morning, your tithes every three days.

chapters.title: Let Justice Roll Down Like Waters
chapters.html:
Amos 5

A Lament for the House of Israel

1Hear this word, which I take up over you as a lament, house of Israel:

2Fallen, no more to rise,
is virgin Israel;
forsaken on her own ground,
with no one to raise her up.

3For this is what the Lord GOD says:
The city that went out a thousand strong
will have a hundred left,
and the one that went out a hundred strong
will have ten left,
for the house of Israel.

Seek Me and Live

4For this is what the LORD says to the house of Israel:
Seek Me and live.

5Do not seek Bethel,
do not go to Gilgal,
and do not cross over to Beersheba;
for Gilgal will surely go into exile,
and Bethel will come to nothing.

6Seek the LORD and live,
or He will rush like fire on the house of Joseph,
and it will devour,
with no one to quench it for Bethel.

7You who turn justice into wormwood
and throw righteousness down to the ground!

8He who made the Pleiades and Orion,
who turns the shadow of death into morning
and darkens day into night,
who calls for the waters of the sea
and pours them out on the face of the earth:
the LORD is His name;

9who makes destruction flash out against the strong,
so that destruction comes upon the fortress.

10They hate the one who reproves at the gate,
and they detest the one who speaks with integrity.

11Therefore, because you trample on the poor
and take a levy of grain from him,
you have built houses of dressed stone,
but you will not live in them;
you have planted pleasant vineyards,
but you will not drink their wine.

12For I know how many are your transgressions
and how mighty your sins,
you who afflict the righteous, who take a bribe,
and turn aside the needy at the gate.

13Therefore the prudent will keep silent at that time,
for it is an evil time.

14Seek good and not evil,
so that you may live;
and so the LORD, the God of hosts, will be with you,
as you have said.

15Hate evil and love good,
and establish justice at the gate;
perhaps the LORD, the God of hosts,
will be gracious to the remnant of Joseph.

16Therefore this is what the LORD, the God of hosts, the Lord, says:
In all the squares there will be wailing,
and in all the streets they will say, "Alas! Alas!"
They will call the farmer to mourning,
and those skilled in lament to wailing.

17In all the vineyards there will be wailing,
for I will pass through among you,
says the LORD.

The Day of the LORD

18Woe to you who long for the day of the LORD!
What will the day of the LORD be to you?
It is darkness, and not light,

19as when a man flees from a lion,
and a bear meets him;
he goes into the house and leans his hand against the wall,
and a snake bites him.

20Is not the day of the LORD darkness, and not light,
gloom with no brightness in it?

21I hate, I reject your feasts,
and I take no pleasure in your sacred assemblies.

22Even if you offer Me burnt offerings
and your grain offerings,
I will not accept them;
I will not look at the peace offerings
of your fattened animals.

23Take away from Me the noise of your songs;
I will not listen to the music of your harps.

24But let justice roll down like waters,
and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream.

25Did you bring Me sacrifices and offerings
in the wilderness forty years, house of Israel?

26You will take up Sikkuth your king
and Kiyyun your images,
the star of your god,
which you made for yourselves,

27and I will send you into exile beyond Damascus,
says the LORD, whose name is the God of hosts.

Notes

  • vv1–3 "a lament… Fallen, no more to rise, is virgin Israel… ten left" — qinah, the funeral song, as David sang this lament over Saul (2 Samuel 1:17); here it is sung over a nation still living. Jeremiah answers it: Again I will build you, and you will be built, virgin Israel (Jeremiah 31:4). A city loses nine in ten, as Isaiah heard of a land where a tenth remains in it (Isaiah 6:13).

  • vv4–6 "Seek Me and live… Gilgal will surely go into exile, and Bethel will come to nothing" — dirshuni, seek Me, the verb of Moses' promise, you will seek the LORD your God, and you will find Him (Deuteronomy 4:29). Ha-Gilgal galoh yigleh: the name of the town sounds out its sentence. Beit-El yihyeh le-aven: the house of God becomes aven, nothing, wickedness, the word Hosea uses to call it Beth-aven (Hosea 4:15). Beersheba lay in the south, Beersheba, which belongs to Judah (1 Kings 19:3), where Abraham called on the name of the LORD (Genesis 21:33) and Isaac built an altar (Genesis 26:25). Yitslach, rush, is the verb of The Spirit of the LORD rushed on him (Judges 14:6), and with no one to quench it is Jeremiah's burn with no one to quench it (Jeremiah 4:4).

  • vv7–9 "You who turn justice into wormwood… who turns the shadow of death into morning" — one verb, hafakh, turn, the verb of the overthrow of Sodom (4:11): they turn justice into la'anah, wormwood, the bitter plant of a root bearing poison and wormwood (Deuteronomy 29:18); the LORD turns tsalmavet, the dark of the valley of the shadow of death (Psalm 23:4), into morning. The hymn breaks into the charge between v7 and v10. Kimah u-khesil, the Pleiades and Orion, are the stars of Job, He made the Bear and Orion, the Pleiades (Job 9:9). Ha-mavlig, who makes flash, is uncertain; the Greek has who apportions ruin.

  • vv10–11 "the one who reproves at the gate… you will not live in them" — the gate was the court. Isaiah too condemns those who lay a snare for the one who reproves at the gate (Isaiah 29:21). Tamim, integrity, is the word for an offering without defect: speech that is whole. Boshaskhem, you trample, is found only here; the Greek has you struck the poor with your fists. The sentence is the law's curse: You will build a house and not live in it (Deuteronomy 28:30), and you will not drink the wine (28:39). Dressed stone is the boast of we will build with dressed stone (Isaiah 9:10).

  • v12 "who take a bribe, and turn aside the needy at the gate" — kofer, a ransom, the price paid for a life: You shall not take a ransom for the life of a murderer (Numbers 35:31), and the bribe Samuel swore he never took, From whose hand have I taken a bribe (1 Samuel 12:3). Turn aside is the law's word, You shall not turn aside the judgment of your needy in his dispute (Exodus 23:6), and the verb of 2:7, turn aside the way of the humble.

  • vv14–15 "the LORD… will be with you, as you have said… perhaps" — they say the LORD is with us, the words of Joshua and Caleb (Numbers 14:9), which Gideon threw back, if the LORD is with us, why has all this found us? (Judges 6:13). Hate evil and love good is the psalm's You who love the LORD, hate evil! (Psalm 97:10). Ulay, perhaps, is all the hope offered, Moses' word on the mountain, Perhaps I can make atonement for your sin (Exodus 32:30).

  • vv16–17 "Alas! Alas!… for I will pass through among you" — ho ho, the cry of mourners. The skilled mourners are Jeremiah's too, send for the skilled women to come (Jeremiah 9:17), and the farmer is called from the field to mourn. E'evor be-qirbekha, I will pass through among you, is the word of the first Passover, I will pass through the land of Egypt that night (Exodus 12:12): this time Israel is the land He passes through.

  • vv18–20 "Woe to you who long for the day of the LORD… darkness, and not light" — hoy, woe, is the cry over the dead, Alas, my brother! (1 Kings 13:30), as ho ho is in v16. The day they long for is turned against them, as in Isaiah, the LORD of hosts has a day against all that is proud (Isaiah 2:12). One man meets three beasts: the lion, the bear, and the snake inside his own house.

  • vv21–24 "I take no pleasure in your sacred assemblies… let justice roll down like waters" — lo ariach, I will not smell, the word of the law's warning, I will not smell your soothing aroma (Leviticus 26:31). Yiggal, roll, is from galal, the verb that named Gilgal, Today I have rolled away the disgrace of Egypt from you (Joshua 5:9). Nachal eitan, an ever-flowing stream, is a wadi that does not run dry, a valley with a flowing stream (Deuteronomy 21:4).

  • vv25–27 "Did you bring Me sacrifices… forty years… You will take up Sikkuth your king and Kiyyun" — Jeremiah asks the same, I did not speak to your fathers… about burnt offerings and sacrifices (Jeremiah 7:22). As pointed, Sikkut and Kiyyun are names found nowhere else, and both carry the vowels of shiqquts, loathsome; Kiyyun stands beside the star of your god. The Greek has the tent of Moloch and the star of your god Raiphan, the words Stephen quotes (Acts 7:42–43); sukkat, the tent of, has the letters of Sikkut. U-nesatem, you will take up, runs on into v27, and I will send you into exile; the Greek has you took up, in the wilderness.

chapters.title: Those at Ease in Zion
chapters.html:
Amos 6

Woe to Those at Ease

1Woe to those at ease in Zion,
and to those who feel secure on the mountain of Samaria,
the notable men of the first among the nations,
to whom the house of Israel comes!

2Cross over to Calneh and see;
go from there to Hamath the great;
then go down to Gath of the Philistines.
Are they better than these kingdoms?
Is their territory greater than your territory?

3You who put far off the day of disaster
and bring near the seat of violence,

4who lie on beds of ivory
and sprawl on their couches,
and eat lambs from the flock
and calves from the fattening stall,

5who strum to the sound of the harp,
and like David devise for themselves instruments of song,

6who drink wine from basins
and anoint themselves with the finest oils,
but are not grieved over the ruin of Joseph!

7Therefore they will now go into exile
at the head of the exiles,
and the feasting of those who sprawl will pass away.

I Abhor the Pride of Jacob

8The Lord GOD has sworn by Himself,
declares the LORD, the God of hosts:
I abhor the pride of Jacob
and hate his strongholds;
I will hand over the city
and all that fills it.

9And it shall come to pass, if ten men are left in one house, that they will die.

10When a man's uncle, the one who burns for him, lifts him up to carry the bones out of the house, he will say to the one in the innermost part of the house, "Is there anyone else with you?" He will say, "No one." Then he will say, "Silence! The name of the LORD must not be mentioned."

11For the LORD is about to command,
and He will strike the great house into fragments
and the small house into splinters.

12Do horses run on the rock?
Does one plow there with oxen?
Yet you have turned justice into poison
and the fruit of righteousness into wormwood.

13You who rejoice in nothing,
who say, "Have we not taken horns for ourselves
by our own strength?"

14For I am about to raise up against you a nation,
house of Israel,
declares the LORD, the God of hosts,
and they will oppress you from Lebo-hamath
to the Wadi of the Arabah.

Notes

  • v1 "those at ease in Zion… the notable men of the first among the nations" — Zion is named with Samaria: Judah is in the woe too. Sha'anannim, at ease, is Isaiah's word, Women at ease, rise up (Isaiah 32:9). Neqvei, notable men, is from the verb of men who had been designated by name (Numbers 1:17). Reshit ha-goyim, the first among the nations, is Balaam's saying, Amalek was first among the nations, but his end is destruction (Numbers 24:20).

  • v2 "Calneh… Hamath the great… Gath of the Philistines" — Isaiah has the Assyrian boast over the same names, Is not Calno like Carchemish? Is not Hamath like Arpad? (Isaiah 10:9). Gath, missing from the Philistine cities of 1:6–8, had been taken by Hazael (2 Kings 12:17). These kingdoms are Israel and Judah of v1, asked whether the fallen cities were any better or any larger.

  • v3 "the seat of violence" — shevet chamas, the sitting of violence: a throne, or a rule. They push away the day of disaster and bring the reign of violence near. The Greek has who draw near and lay hold of false sabbaths: shevet has the letters of shabbat.

  • vv4–6 "beds of ivory… couches… wine from basins… the finest oils" — the bed and the couch of 3:12, where all that is rescued is the corner of a bed and a piece of a couch. Mizraq, basin, is the vessel of the altar, one silver basin of seventy shekels (Numbers 7:13); here it is filled with wine. Marbeq, the fattening stall, is where the woman of Endor kept a fattened calf (1 Samuel 28:24). Reshit shemanim, the first of oils, says reshit again, as in v1.

  • v5 "like David devise for themselves instruments of song" — David spoke of the instruments I made for praise (1 Chronicles 23:5), and the Levites stood with the instruments of David (2 Chronicles 29:26). Chashvu lahem can be devise for themselves or count themselves, as David at his instruments. Ha-poretim, who strum, is found only here.

  • vv6–7 "not grieved over the ruin of Joseph… the feasting of those who sprawl will pass away" — shever Yosef, the breaking of Joseph, the north. Mirzach, feasting, is the word of Do not enter the house of mourning (Jeremiah 16:5): there a gathering for the dead, here a feast for the living, while Joseph breaks. Be-rosh golim, at the head of the exiles: the first among the nations, anointed with the first of the oils, go into exile first.

  • v8 "sworn by Himself… I abhor the pride of Jacob… I will hand over the city" — be-nafsho, by Himself, as in The LORD of hosts has sworn by Himself (Jeremiah 51:14). Ge'on Ya'aqov, the pride of Jacob, is what the psalm sings, the pride of Jacob, whom He loves (Psalm 47:4). Ve-hisgarti, I will hand over, is the verb of Gaza and Tyre, who handed whole peoples over to Edom (1:6, 9).

  • vv9–10 "his uncle, the one who burns for him… Silence! The name of the LORD must not be mentioned" — dodo, his uncle, the kinsman who carries out the dead, as Aaron's uncle's sons carried out Nadab and Abihu (Leviticus 10:4). Mesarefo, the one who burns for him: the burning made in honor of the dead, a very great fire in his honor (2 Chronicles 16:14), or the burning of the body, as at Jabesh, They came to Jabesh and burned them there (1 Samuel 31:12). Has, Silence!, is Eglon's word (Judges 3:19). The law said The name of other gods you shall not mention (Exodus 23:13); here it is the LORD's name that must not be said.

  • v12 "Do horses run on the rock? Does one plow there with oxen?" — the second question has no rock of its own; there takes it from the first: no one plows rock with oxen. The Greek has will they keep silent among mares? Rosh and la'anah, poison and wormwood, are the pair of a root bearing poison and wormwood (Deuteronomy 29:18); Hosea has justice spring up like poison (Hosea 10:4), and 5:7 here has it turned into wormwood.

  • vv13–14 "who rejoice in nothing… taken horns… from Lebo-hamath to the Wadi of the Arabah" — lo davar, nothing, and qarnayim, horns, are also the names of towns: Lo-debar (2 Samuel 9:4) and Ashteroth-karnaim (Genesis 14:5). The Hebrew points lo davar as words, not as the town, and the Greek reads both as words. Horns were Joseph's in Moses' blessing, his horns are the horns of the wild ox (Deuteronomy 33:17). The nation's march runs the length of what Jeroboam won, who restored the border of Israel from Lebo-hamath to the Sea of the Arabah (2 Kings 14:25).

chapters.title: I Was No Prophet
chapters.html:
Amos 7

Locusts and Fire

1This is what the Lord GOD showed me: He was forming locusts when the late crop was beginning to come up, the late crop after the king's mowing.

2When they had finished eating the grass of the land, I said, "Lord GOD, forgive, please! How can Jacob stand? He is so small."

3The LORD relented concerning this. "It shall not be," said the LORD.

4This is what the Lord GOD showed me: the Lord GOD was calling to contend by fire, and it devoured the great deep and was devouring the portion.

5I said, "Lord GOD, stop, please! How can Jacob stand? He is so small."

6The LORD relented concerning this. "This too shall not be," said the Lord GOD.

The Plumb Line

7This is what He showed me: the Lord was standing beside a wall made by a plumb line, with a plumb line in His hand.

8The LORD said to me, "What do you see, Amos?" I said, "A plumb line." Then the Lord said, "I am about to set a plumb line among My people Israel; I will never again pass them by.

9The high places of Isaac will be made desolate,
and the sanctuaries of Israel laid waste,
and I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword."

Amaziah the Priest of Bethel

10Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent word to Jeroboam king of Israel: "Amos has conspired against you among the house of Israel; the land cannot bear all his words.

11For this is what Amos says: 'Jeroboam will die by the sword, and Israel will surely go into exile from its land.'"

12Amaziah said to Amos, "Seer, go, run away to the land of Judah. Earn your bread there, and prophesy there.

13But never prophesy again at Bethel, for it is the king's sanctuary and a royal house."

14Amos answered Amaziah, "I was no prophet, nor a prophet's son; I was a herdsman and a tender of sycamore figs.

15But the LORD took me from following the flock, and the LORD said to me, 'Go, prophesy to My people Israel.'

16Now hear the word of the LORD. You say, 'Do not prophesy against Israel, and do not preach against the house of Isaac.'

17Therefore this is what the LORD says:
'Your wife will become a prostitute in the city,
and your sons and your daughters will fall by the sword,
and your land will be divided up with a measuring line;
you yourself will die on unclean ground,
and Israel will surely go into exile from its land.'"

Notes

  • v1 "the late crop after the king's mowing" — leqesh, the late crop, and gizzei ha-melekh, the king's mowing, a phrase found only here: the cut taken for the king, and the locusts come for the growth after it. The Greek reads gizzei as a name: one young locust, Gog the king.

  • vv2–3, 5–6 "Lord GOD, forgive, please! How can Jacob stand? He is so small… The LORD relented" — mi yaqum Ya'aqov, word for word who will Jacob stand; the Greek has who will raise Jacob up? Amos pleads for the people he was sent against, and the LORD relents, nicham, as on the mountain, The LORD relented of the evil He had said He would do to His people (Exodus 32:14). At the second vision Amos no longer asks forgiveness, only stop.

  • v4 "calling to contend by fire… devoured the great deep and was devouring the portion" — la-riv, to contend, the word of a case at law (Hosea 4:1). Tehom rabbah, the great deep, is the deep of the flood, when all the fountains of the great deep were split open (Genesis 7:11): a fire that eats up the deep. Ha-cheleq, the portion, is the allotted land, each family's share.

  • vv7–8 "a wall made by a plumb line, with a plumb line in His hand… I will never again pass them by" — anakh, four times in two verses and nowhere else. Plumb line follows the picture of a wall tested for true; the Greek has adamas, a hard metal: a wall of adamant, and adamant in His hand. Lo osif od avor lo, I will never again pass them by, is the verb of overlooking, it is his glory to overlook an offense (Proverbs 19:11). In 5:17 the LORD said I will pass through among you; now He will no longer pass them by.

  • vv9, 16 "the high places of Isaac… the house of Isaac" — Yischaq, spelled with sin where the name usually has tsade, as in Jeremiah 33:26 and His oath to Isaac (Psalm 105:9). So spelled, it carries the sound of sachaq, laugh, and the Greek reads it so: the altars of laughter will be made desolate.

  • vv10–11 "Amos has conspired against you… Jeroboam will die by the sword" — Amos said I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword (v9); Amaziah reports it as Jeroboam will die by the sword. Jeroboam lay down with his fathers, and it was his son Zechariah against whom Shallum son of Jabesh conspired (2 Kings 14:29; 15:10). Qashar, conspired, is the word of that plot.

  • vv12–13 "Seer, go, run away to the land of Judah… the king's sanctuary and a royal house" — Earn your bread there is word for word eat bread there. Bethel, the house of God, is called by its priest the king's sanctuary and a royal house, and God is not named in his words.

  • v14 "I was no prophet, nor a prophet's son" — lo navi anokhi ve-lo ven navi anokhi, with no verb: not a prophet I, and not a prophet's son I. It can be past, I was no prophet until the LORD took me (v15), as the Greek has it, I was not a prophet; or present, I am no prophet, refusing to be one who earns his bread by prophecy (v12). A prophet's son is one of the prophets' guilds, like the sons of the prophets who were at Bethel (2 Kings 2:3). Boles shiqmim, a tender of sycamore figs, is found only here; the sycamore grew in the lowland, as plentiful as the sycamore trees of the lowland (1 Kings 10:27). The Greek has a goatherd.

  • v15 "the LORD took me from following the flock" — va-yiqqacheni YHWH me-acharei ha-tson, the words said to David, I took you from the pasture, from following the sheep (2 Samuel 7:8).

  • vv16–17 "do not preach against the house of Isaac… Israel will surely go into exile from its land" — tattif, preach, is the verb drip, as Ezekiel was told to preach against the sanctuaries (Ezekiel 21:2). The sentence ends with Amaziah's own report of Amos (v11), word for word: what the priest called a conspiracy, the LORD says again. Unclean ground is a foreign land, as Hosea says in Assyria they will eat unclean food (Hosea 9:3).

chapters.title: The End Has Come
chapters.html:
Amos 8

A Basket of Summer Fruit

1This is what the Lord GOD showed me: a basket of summer fruit.

2He said, "What do you see, Amos?" I said, "A basket of summer fruit." Then the LORD said to me, "The end has come upon My people Israel; I will never again pass them by.

3The songs of the temple will turn to howling on that day,
declares the Lord GOD.
So many corpses!
They are flung out everywhere.
Silence!"

When Will the Sabbath Be Over?

4Hear this, you who trample the needy
and put an end to the poor of the land,

5saying, "When will the new moon be over,
so that we may sell grain,
and the sabbath,
so that we may open up the grain,
making the ephah small and the shekel great,
and cheating with false scales,

6buying the poor for silver
and the needy for a pair of sandals,
and selling the chaff of the grain?"

7The LORD has sworn by the pride of Jacob:
I will never forget any of their deeds.

8Shall not the land tremble for this,
and everyone who lives in it mourn?
All of it will rise like the Nile,
be tossed about, and sink again,
like the Nile of Egypt.

A Famine of the Word

9And it shall come to pass on that day,
declares the Lord GOD,
that I will make the sun go down at noon
and darken the earth in broad daylight.

10I will turn your feasts into mourning
and all your songs into a lament;
I will put sackcloth on every waist
and baldness on every head;
I will make it like the mourning for an only son,
and its end like a bitter day.

11Days are coming,
declares the Lord GOD,
when I will send a famine on the land,
not a famine for bread or a thirst for water,
but for hearing the words of the LORD.

12They will stagger from sea to sea
and from the north to the east;
they will roam about to seek the word of the LORD,
and they will not find it.

13On that day the fair young women
and the young men will faint for thirst,

14those who swear by the guilt of Samaria,
and say, "As your god lives, Dan,"
and, "As the way of Beersheba lives";
they will fall and never rise again.

Notes

  • vv1–2 "a basket of summer fruit… The end has come" — kelub qayits, and the answer, ba ha-qets: qayits, the fruit of the last harvest, and qets, end, sound nearly alike. Jeremiah's first vision turns the same way, on a branch of an almond tree, shaqed, and I am watching, shoqed (Jeremiah 1:11–12), and Ezekiel cries An end! The end has come (Ezekiel 7:2). Kelub, basket, is the cage of Jeremiah 5:27, Like a cage full of birds. I will never again pass them by repeats 7:8.

  • v3 "The songs of the temple will turn to howling… Silence!" — shirot heikhal, the songs of the temple; with other vowels the same letters are the singing women of the palace, and heikhal is both temple and palace. The Greek has the ceiling panels of the temple will wail. Has, Silence!, is the hush of 6:10, among the dead.

  • vv4–5 "put an end to the poor… When will the new moon be over… and the sabbath" — lashbit, put an end to, is from shavat, the root of shabbat: they would make the poor cease, and cannot wait for the sabbath to cease. Ha-sho'afim, you who trample, is the word of 2:7. Sell grain… open up the grain are the verbs of Joseph in the famine, who opened all that was in them and sold grain (Genesis 41:56); these sellers open to cheat.

  • vv5–6 "the ephah small and the shekel great… a pair of sandals" — a small measure for the grain and a heavy weight for the buyer's silver: the two kinds of weights, a large and a small of the law (Deuteronomy 25:13), and the false scales of Hosea 12:7. In 2:6 they sell the righteous for silver, and the needy for a pair of sandals; here they buy them at the same price.

  • v7 "The LORD has sworn by the pride of Jacob" — bi-g'on Ya'aqov, the words of 6:8, where He swore by Himself, I abhor the pride of Jacob. Here He swears by it: by the pride He will not forget, or by Himself under a name, as Samuel calls Him the Enduring One of Israel (1 Samuel 15:29) and as He swore to Abraham, By Myself I have sworn (Genesis 22:16).

  • v8 "rise like the Nile… and sink again, like the Nile of Egypt" — the Nile rises over its land each year and falls again; the whole land will heave like it. Ka-or, like the Nile, is written without the y of ye'or; 9:5 gives the same line with the word in full. The read form, ve-nishqe'ah, and sink, is followed.

  • vv9–10 "the sun go down at noon… like the mourning for an only son" — the law's curse, You will grope at noon as the blind man gropes in darkness (Deuteronomy 28:29), and Jeremiah's mother of seven, her sun has gone down while it was still day (Jeremiah 15:9): the day of the LORD as darkness, and not light (5:18). Evel yachid, the mourning for an only son, is Jeremiah's make mourning as for an only son, a most bitter lament (Jeremiah 6:26). The Greek has the mourning for a beloved one, its word for Isaac in your son — your beloved one (Genesis 22:2). Baldness is the mourner's shaved head the law forbade, a bald patch between your eyes for the dead (Deuteronomy 14:1).

  • vv11–12 "a famine… for hearing the words of the LORD… They will stagger" — the law said a person does not live on bread alone, but on everything that comes out of the mouth of the LORD (Deuteronomy 8:3), and in Eli's days The word of the LORD was rare (1 Samuel 3:1). Na'u, stagger, is the verb of 4:8, where cities staggered to one city for water; yeshotetu, roam about, is Jeremiah's Roam through the streets of Jerusalem (Jeremiah 5:1).

  • v14 "the guilt of Samaria… As your god lives, Dan… the way of Beersheba" — ashmat Shomron, the guilt of Samaria, its calf, as Hosea says, Your calf is rejected, Samaria (Hosea 8:5). Ashima, the god the men of Hamath made in Samaria's towns after its fall (2 Kings 17:30), has nearly the same letters; the Greek has the propitiation of Samaria. The other calf stood at Dan: He set the one in Bethel, and the other he put in Dan (1 Kings 12:29). Derekh, the way, is the pilgrim road to Beersheba (5:5); the Greek has As your god lives, Beersheba. They will fall and never rise again is the lament of 5:2.

chapters.title: The Fallen Booth of David
chapters.html:
Amos 9

The Lord Beside the Altar

1I saw the Lord standing beside the altar, and He said:
Strike the capitals so that the thresholds shake,
and shatter them on the heads of them all;
the last of them I will kill with the sword.
Not one of them will get away;
not one of them will escape.

2If they dig down into Sheol,
from there My hand will take them;
if they climb up to the heavens,
from there I will bring them down.

3If they hide on the top of Carmel,
from there I will search them out and take them;
if they hide from My eyes on the floor of the sea,
from there I will command the serpent, and it will bite them.

4If they go into captivity before their enemies,
from there I will command the sword, and it will kill them;
I will set My eyes on them
for harm and not for good.

5The Lord GOD of hosts,
He who touches the earth and it melts,
and all who live in it mourn;
all of it rises like the Nile
and sinks like the Nile of Egypt;

6who builds His upper rooms in the heavens
and founds His vault upon the earth;
who calls for the waters of the sea
and pours them out on the face of the earth:
the LORD is His name.

The Sinful Kingdom

7Are you not like the Cushites to Me,
sons of Israel?
declares the LORD.
Did I not bring Israel up from the land of Egypt,
and the Philistines from Caphtor,
and the Arameans from Kir?

8The eyes of the Lord GOD are on the sinful kingdom,
and I will destroy it from the face of the ground;
except that I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob,
declares the LORD.

9For I am about to command,
and I will shake the house of Israel among all the nations
as one shakes with a sieve,
and not a pebble will fall to the ground.

10All the sinners of My people will die by the sword,
those who say,
"Disaster will not come near us or meet us."

I Will Raise It Up

11On that day I will raise up
the fallen booth of David,
and wall up its breaches,
and raise up its ruins,
and rebuild it as in the days of old,

12so that they may possess the remnant of Edom
and all the nations over whom My name is called,
declares the LORD, who does this.

13Days are coming,
declares the LORD,
when the plowman will overtake the reaper,
and the one who treads grapes the one who sows the seed;
the mountains will drip sweet wine,
and all the hills will melt.

14I will restore the fortunes of My people Israel;
they will rebuild the ruined cities and live in them;
they will plant vineyards and drink their wine;
they will make gardens and eat their fruit.

15I will plant them on their land,
and they will never again be uprooted
from the land I have given them,
says the LORD your God.

Notes

  • v1 "I saw the Lord standing beside the altar… Strike the capitals" — the fifth vision, and the only one that does not begin This is what… showed me (7:1, 4, 7; 8:1), and here Amos does not plead. Who is told to strike is not said. Kaftor, capital, the top of a pillar, is the word of the lampstand's bulbs (Exodus 25:31) and the name of Caphtor in v7. The altar is not named; 3:14 named the altars of Bethel. The Greek has Strike the mercy seat.

  • vv2–4 "If they dig down into Sheol… for harm and not for good" — the psalm's comfort turned around: If I go up to the heavens, You are there; if I make my bed in Sheol, You are there (Psalm 139:8). The serpent is the one that bit the man in his own house (5:19). I will set My eyes on them for harm and not for good is the reverse of Jeremiah's promise, I will set My eyes on them for good… I will plant them and not uproot them (Jeremiah 24:6), and Jeremiah has the threat too, I will watch over them for harm and not for good (Jeremiah 44:27).

  • vv5–6 "He who touches the earth and it melts… the LORD is His name" — the hymn takes up two lines already heard: the earth rising and sinking like the Nile (8:8), and who calls for the waters of the sea and pours them out on the face of the earth (5:8). Aguddato, His vault, is uncertain: agudah is a thing bound together, a bunch of hyssop (Exodus 12:22); the Greek has His promise.

  • v7 "Are you not like the Cushites to Me… the Philistines from Caphtor, and the Arameans from Kir?" — Cush is the land of Genesis 2:13 and of Moses' wife, the Cushite woman he had married (Numbers 12:1); the Greek has the sons of the Ethiopians. The Philistines are the Caphtorim, who came out of Caphtor (Deuteronomy 2:23), and the Arameans, brought from Kir, are sent back to it (1:5). The exodus, the ground of Only you have I known (3:2), is set beside the LORD's other moves of peoples.

  • v8 "except that I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob" — efes ki, except that, and hashmed ashmid, the verb doubled, utterly destroy. After the perhaps of 5:15, perhaps the LORD… will be gracious to the remnant of Joseph, the line turns: the kingdom will go, and the house of Jacob will not go with it entirely.

  • vv9–10 "as one shakes with a sieve, and not a pebble will fall… Disaster will not come near us" — kevarah, sieve, is found only here. Tseror is a pebble, as in not even a pebble is found there (2 Samuel 17:13), and also a bundle, as in the bundle of the living (1 Samuel 25:29): the sieve holds back every stone, or lets no grain of the people fall lost; the Greek has no fragment will fall. Taggish, come near, is the verb of 6:3: they bring near the seat of violence and say disaster will not come near.

  • v11 "the fallen booth of David" — sukkat David ha-nofelet. Sukkah is a shelter of branches, Isaiah's shelter in a vineyard (Isaiah 1:8), the booths of the feast (Leviticus 23:42); sukkat has the letters of Sikkuth in 5:26. Ha-nofelet… aqim, fallen… I will raise up, answers the lament, Fallen, no more to rise, is virgin Israel… with no one to raise her up (5:2). The Hebrew's pronouns change three times: their breaches, his ruins, rebuild it. The Greek has the tent of David.

  • v12 "so that they may possess the remnant of Edom and all the nations over whom My name is called" — over whom My name is called is the law's the name of the LORD is called over you (Deuteronomy 28:10). The Greek reads differently: so that the rest of mankind may seek, and all the nations over whom My name is called. Edom and adam, mankind, have nearly the same letters, as do yirshu, possess, and yidreshu, seek. James quotes the Greek at the gathering in Jerusalem, of the nations coming in (Acts 15:16–17). The Hebrew, the text here, has Edom, the brother of 1:11.

  • v13 "the plowman will overtake the reaper… the mountains will drip sweet wine" — the blessing of the law, Your threshing will last until the grape harvest, and the grape harvest until the sowing (Leviticus 26:5): one harvest runs into the next. Joel has the dripping mountains as well (Joel 3:18). Titmogagnah, will melt, is the verb of v5, where the earth melted at His touch.

  • vv14–15 "rebuild the ruined cities and live in them… drink their wine… says the LORD your God" — 5:11 undone: you have built houses of dressed stone, but you will not live in them… but you will not drink their wine. Shavti et shevut, I will restore the fortunes, is Jeremiah's I will restore your fortunes (Jeremiah 29:14), and I will plant them… never again be uprooted is his I will plant them and not uproot them (Jeremiah 24:6). The book's last words are Elohekha, your God, as in prepare to meet your God (4:12).
